note: Read on the Legislation and Legal Opinion Commission's site (lloc.gov.bh), whose English texts are Word files (their text was taken out to be read). Majority: null. The Civil Code (Legislative Decree No. 19 of 2001) doesn't state the age: arts. 73 to 75 speak of a minor with or without discretion (under seven lacks it) until 'legal age', set elsewhere; the law that fixes it (guardianship over property) wasn't found on lloc.gov.bh by its categories or by id, and a web search found only unsourced secondary claims of 21 and 18 (2026-10-31). Work: 15. Labour Law for the Private Sector (Law No. 36 of 2012): it is prohibited to employ anyone under fifteen; a juvenile is 15 to 18, at most six hours a day, never at night or on rest days, with the parents' or guardians' approval, a medical check and notice to the Ministry: not held. The law has 4 amendments listed (2021 among them) that weren't compared. Performers: barred, the reading being that the law has no exception for young performers or artistic work. Service: null. No conscription law was found or looked for in the time; the Bahrain Defence Force's own law wasn't read.

sources.title: Legislation and Legal Opinion Commission (Bahrain): Law No. (36) of 2012 promulgating the Labour Law for the Private Sector (English)
sources.said: a juvenile means every person of fifteen years of age but not exceeding eighteen years of age ... It is prohibited to employ anyone who is less than fifteen years of age.

sources.title: Legislation and Legal Opinion Commission (Bahrain): Legislative Decree No. (19) of 2001 promulgating the Civil Code (English)
sources.said: A minor shall possess discretion from the discretion age until attaining legal age.
